title: Mining Statistically Significant Substrings Based on the Chi-Square Measure
review_status: full-text audit complete; five-symbol ODI quantization and same-sequence probability estimates, 989,819-record click benchmark, exact top-1 result, runtime, approximation ratios, and absent held-out/multiple-testing calibration checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2010-02-23, v2 2010-03-06; arXiv comments state to appear in PAKDD 2010
evidence_note: On ODI runs, five outcome bins and probabilities are estimated from the same 425-innings career record; top/bottom periods have reported averages 84.31 (20 innings) and 21.89 (9 innings). On a 989,819-record click sequence both heuristics are exact at top-1; ARLM/AGMM take 40/3 hours versus naive 75+ hours and blocking 52 hours. No varying top-k run is reported on the click dataset due to runtime. Synthetic approximation ratios exceed 0.96 in tested settings. The paper does not report held-out calibration or correction for scanning multiple overlapping substrings.

title: Bayesian Data Cleaning for Web Data
review_status: full-text audit complete; probabilistic model, manually inspected source data, injected corruption types/rates, ground-truth comparison, correction/false-positive tradeoff, runtime, and one-domain limitations checked
sections_checked: Section 4 Bayesian generative and maximum-entropy error models
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2012-04-17; v1 is a six-page arXiv paper, with no venue asserted in this audit
evidence_note: Evaluation uses around 10,000 crawled used-car records from Google Base, manually inspected as clean before synthetic spelling/replacement/deletion corruption at 0.1%-5%. At 1% noise, the paper reports 357 injected errors and a best net gain of 87 clean values at parameter 3.0; combined features correct >31% of errors while compared CFD methods learn no CFD. False positives are reported at no more than 11 tuples in these parameter experiments, and increasing the likelihood weight reduces both false positives and corrections. This is controlled one-schema evidence, not naturally occurring multi-domain web-noise validation.

title: Recursive Mechanism: Towards Node Differential Privacy and Unrestricted Joins [Full Version, Draft 0.1]
review_status: full-text audit complete; empirical-sensitivity error analysis, node/edge privacy distinction, synthetic and real graph comparisons, motif-specific failures, and draft-versus-proceedings caveat checked
sections_checked: Sections 3-5: empirical sensitivity and recursive mechanism/error bounds
Section 6.1 subgraph-counting experimental setup and results, Figures 4-7
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2013-04-17; arXiv record says full-version Draft 0.1; PDF notes a different version accepted at SIGMOD 2013
evidence_note: The method releases approximate linear statistics over positive relational-algebra results with node- or edge-DP, with error related to empirical sensitivity. Experiments include random synthetic graphs and seven real graphs. The paper reports best accuracy among comparators for its edge-private triangle-counting experiments; node-private 2-star and 2-triangle relative errors are high because one node affects many motifs, though the relative error decreases with graph size. These workload/data-dependent errors bound, rather than refute, the privacy result.

title: Opening the Black Boxes in Data Flow Optimization
review_status: full-text re-audit complete; reconciled with prior batch 6 audit; static-analysis properties, four handcrafted evaluation tasks, plan enumeration, measured plan runtime comparisons, and limitations checked
sections_checked: Sections 5-6 property discovery and plan enumeration
Section 7 evaluation setup and four workloads
TPC-H Q7/Q15, clickstream and PubMed text-mining plan/runtime results
Static-code-analysis coverage, enumeration overhead and conclusion/future work
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2012-08-01; PVLDB Vol. 5 No. 11, pp. 1256-1267 (2012), verified from arXiv journal reference
evidence_note: Rechecked the full text and prior batch 6 notes. A Stratosphere prototype statically analyzes UDF read/write properties to reorder black-box operators. Four handcrafted tasks include modified TPC-H queries, biomedical PubMed text mining and clickstream processing. The best text-mining plan is nearly an order of magnitude faster than the worst sampled plan; the best TPC-H Q15 plan is 1.4x faster than the implemented flow. SCA recovers almost all manually annotated alternatives; plan enumeration takes under 1,654 ms. The authors leave cost/selectivity estimation and better search-space pruning as future work.

title: Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL
review_status: full-text re-audit complete; reconciled with prior batch 44 audit; implementation scope, SIBENCH, modified DBT-2++ configurations, RUBiS throughput/failure results, and CPU/disk workload differences checked
sections_checked: Sections 5-7 PostgreSQL SSI integration and optimizations
Section 8.2 DBT-2++ CPU- and disk-bound workloads
Section 8.3 RUBiS and Section 8.4 deferrable transactions
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2012-08-21; PVLDB Vol. 5 No. 12, pp. 1850-1861 (2012), verified from arXiv journal reference
evidence_note: Rechecked the full text and prior batch 44 notes. PostgreSQL 9.1 SSI is tested with SIBENCH, modified DBT-2++ and RUBiS. RUBiS reports 422 requests/s for SSI vs 435 for SI and 208 for S2PL, with serialization failures 0.03%, 0.004%, and 0.76% respectively. In-memory DBT-2++ shows 5% slowdown vs SI; disk-bound SSI is indistinguishable from SI and failure rates stay below 0.25%. SIBENCH reports 10-20% CPU overhead for dependency tracking before read-only optimizations. Benchmarks are system/hardware-era specific.

title: Analysis and Study of Incremental DBSCAN Clustering Algorithm
review_status: full-text re-audit complete; reconciled with prior batch 44 audit; proposed incremental pseudocode, illustrative examples, lack of dataset-backed runtime/quality evaluation, terminology inconsistencies, and PDF/arXiv date discrepancy checked; excluded from positive effect evidence
sections_checked: Sections 2-3 proposed incremental algorithm and threshold model
PDF journal masthead and reference list
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2014-06-18; PDF embeds International Journal of Enterprise Computing and Business Systems Vol. 1 Issue 2 July 2011 masthead, while the arXiv record lists no journal reference; discrepancy left unresolved
evidence_note: Rechecked the full text and prior batch 44 notes. The body gives a threshold-comparison recipe and toy examples but no dataset-backed runtime or clustering-quality results and no measured crossover threshold. It claims incremental DBSCAN is faster, yet lacks reported quantitative measurements; text/pseudocode also shifts between DBSCAN and K-means/new-item insertion. Treated as a negative-control evidence disposition only, not a result about the general DBSCAN literature.
